text:
maya (support): Hey team, customer AcmeCorp (j.smith) reporting streaming API disconnects and lots of partial outputs. They say it happens after ~60s of silence from the server. stacktrace attached. :thinking:

j.smith (AcmeCorp): They see the stream stop sending new chunks mid-response. Sometimes curl shows half the JSON and then connection drops. This broke our chat widget.

maya (support): Thanks for the report. Can you paste the raw curl you used to repro? Also which edge/proxy are you hitting (ALB / Cloudflare / NLB / custom nginx)?

j.smith (AcmeCorp): Request flow is browser -> Cloudflare -> ALB -> Redwood-hosted API. Using SSE (text/event-stream). We tried server-side and client-side. Reproable with curl too. Here's what we run:

```bash
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\\  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\\  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat?model=redwood-1"
```

eli (eng-runtime): :eyes: a couple suspects: proxy buffering + idle timeouts. ALB default idle timeout is 60s. Cloudflare may buffer and try to reassemble chunked responses. Also nginx/Envoy in front of the runtime can buffer by default.

maya (support): Customer saw partial output (valid JSON fragment) then connection reset by peer. That matches proxy closing idle connections.

alex (ops-oncall): Quick checklist for debugging from ops side:
- confirm upstream (ALB) idle timeout
- check Cloudflare "Origin" settings (disable buffering / enable WebSockets / set "Cache" to bypass)
- look for nginx `proxy_buffering` and `proxy_read_timeout` values
- for Envoy, check `stream_idle_timeout` and `common_http_protocol_options.idle_timeout`

eli (eng-runtime): For streaming SSE we recommend clients send periodic keepalive comments from the server when user-level tokens are quiet, e.g. every 15s send `:heartbeat\n\n` comments so proxies don't consider connection idle. Also you can set chunked flush after each event.

maya (support): Asked customer if they can try adding keepalives. j.smith, can you toggle a setting to force server keepalives?

j.smith (AcmeCorp): We can't change backend. We control Cloudflare and ALB settings.

eli (eng-runtime): Ok, then try increasing the ALB idle timeout > 120s (up to 4000s), and on Cloudflare set the origin to bypass caching and disable HTTP/2 multiplexing to origin (Cloudflare sometimes buffers in HTTP/2). Also set "Response Buffering" off if using Cloudflare Workers or set `cache: no-cache` headers.

alex (ops-oncall): For nginx in front of the app (if any): add `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 300s; proxy_send_timeout 300s;` and set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on responses. Example in upstream location block:

```nginx
location /streams/ {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_read_timeout 300s;
  proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no;
}
```

eli (eng-runtime): For Envoy add the following to the route config if using HTTP/1 streaming:
- `stream_idle_timeout: 0s` (or large)
- adjust `idle_timeout` in cluster config
And ensure `max_stream_duration` isn't truncating.

maya (support): Customer tried ALB idle timeout increase already to 120s but still saw drops around ~120s. Cloudflare may still be interfering.

j.smith (AcmeCorp): After ALB increase, we still see drops, and sometimes the stream resumes if the client reconnects. But state was lost (no resume tokens).

eli (eng-runtime): Two things here: 1) check if Cloudflare is terminating HTTP/2 to the client and speaking HTTP/1 to origin or vice versa — that can affect chunking semantics. 2) For immediate mitigation, implement client auto-reconnect with idempotent resume tokens or soft-replay. We don't have server-side resume for streaming responses today, so consumer should re-request and dedupe.

maya (support): Can you collect a repro capture? Ask customer to run this to show whether chunks are arriving progressively or buffered until close:

```bash
curl -v -N --no-buffer -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \\\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \\\  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat?model=redwood-1' | sed -u 's/^/[OUT] /'
```

and also run `tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 443` on the origin side if possible to show TLS frames (ops).

support-bot: Incident template created: #INC-3187 streaming disconnects (linked).

alex (ops-oncall): I checked ALB logs — connection closes at the client side with ELB status code 502 sometimes, and 504 for idle at ALB. Cloudflare logs show HTTP 524 (timeout) in front of our origin for several requests. That indicates Cloudflare waiting for backend response and closing.

eli (eng-runtime): 524 from Cloudflare definitely means Cloudflare considered origin timed out. Cloudflare default 100s wait? If so, increasing ALB to >100s won't matter because CF will kill earlier. CF suggests using heartbeat or switch to WebSockets or use their "long polling" configuration.

j.smith (AcmeCorp): Is there a recommended config we can use specifically for Cloudflare + ALB?

eli (eng-runtime): Recommended for Cloudflare in front of SSE: 
- Use "Bypass cache" page rule for streaming endpoints.
- Disable HTTP/2 to origin (sometimes helps chunked delivery). In Cloudflare dashboard: Network -> HTTP/2 -> toggle off for origin.
- Enable "Always Online" off.
- If still flaky, consider switching Cloudflare to a TCP proxy (spectrum) or use NLB in front of origin to preserve raw TCP.

maya (support): Also remind customer to check client-side: browsers will close idle SSE if page is backgrounded on some mobile browsers. Confirmed?

j.smith (AcmeCorp): Most repros from server-side load tests using curl. Not browsers.

eli (eng-runtime): For reproducible test, run a small node script that opens SSE and logs timestamps per event to verify keepalive behavior. Example:

```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat?model=redwood-1', {
    headers: { Accept: 'text/event-stream', Authorization: 'Bearer ' + process.env.T },
  });
  res.body.on('data', chunk => { console.log('chunk', chunk.toString()); });
})();
```

maya (support): Customer executed the curl --no-buffer test and pasted output. They show the first 2 events streaming, then a gap, then the connection closed with `Connection reset by peer`.

j.smith (AcmeCorp): Paste of curl output:
```
* Connected to api.redwood.example (1.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/streams/chat?model=redwood-1 HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Accept: text/event-stream
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
< transfer-encoding: chunked
< x-accel-buffering: no

[OUT] data: {"delta":"Hello"}
[OUT] data: {"delta":" world"}
# ~70s of silence in TCP
* Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
```

eli (eng-runtime): Silence means server didn't produce keepalive. But if Cloudflare or ALB closes for idle, we'll see that reset. Given you saw CF 524 earlier, CF likely killed the origin at ~100s.

alex (ops-oncall): Short-term mitigations for customer:
- Increase ALB idle timeout to something > Cloudflare timeout (if you can change Cloudflare, adjust there).
- Configure Cloudflare page rule to bypass caching and allow long responses.
- If using Cloudflare, enable "WebSockets" and consider using WebSocket wrapper for streaming (ensures less buffering) or use Cloudflare Workers to proxy raw streaming.
- For now, set a server keepalive at 15s to prevent idle.

maya (support): I've written a recommended checklist for the customer and added it to the ticket: reproduction steps, curl commands, ops logs to gather, and short-term workarounds.

j.smith (AcmeCorp): We'll try disabling Cloudflare buffering and add keepalives. If still flakey we'll recreate behind NLB instead of ALB.

eli (eng-runtime): Follow-up action for eng-runtime: we should detect when client's connection path includes proxies known to buffer (Cloudflare, Akamai) and respond with a small heartbeat every 10s by default for SSE on hosted plan. Create design doc?

maya (support): Filed feature request: STREAM-74 heartbeat for hosted streaming endpoints.

support-bot: Ticket #INC-3187 updated with latest logs and CF/ALB evidence.

maya (support): Closing loop for now — customer will try suggested Cloudflare + ALB changes and report back. If they still see disconnects we'll escalate to eng-runtime to add server-side heartbeat or consider explicit header signals to disable buffering in upstream proxies. :white_check_mark:
